extracted.intended_audience: clinicians and researchers conducting measurement validation and inter-rater reliability studies across medical, allied-health, and educational contexts
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, reporting, and evaluating studies of inter-rater and intra-rater reliability (and related validity) for clinical, observational, and assessment instruments; includes choice of agreement statistics, study design elements, and reporting conventions. Focus spans instrument validation, rater training, and methodological quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Cohen's kappa for categorical agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure agreement between two raters for categorical/nominal judgments using Cohen's kappa (κ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout many studies to quantify inter- and intra-rater agreement for categorical diagnoses/stages; interpretive language in texts uses qualitative bands (e.g., slight, fair, moderate, substantial, almost perfect). Report κ values and confidence intervals where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fleiss' kappa for multi-rater categorical agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure agreement among multiple raters for categorical decisions using Fleiss' kappa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when more than two raters or for sector-by-sector agreement as in image interpretation studies; report κ and context (number of raters, categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa (linear and quadratic) for ordinal ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use weighted kappa statistics (linear and quadratic weightings) to assess inter-rater agreement on ordinal/graded scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for rating scales like Eftedal and Brubakk grading or Asher-McDade ratings; specify weighting scheme (linear vs quadratic) and report weighted κ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for continuous or scale measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to quantify intra- and inter-rater reliability for continuous or multi-item scale scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ICC model (e.g., ICC(2,1), ICC(3,1), ICC(2,3)), report ICC with confidence intervals, and use for test-retest, interrater, and intrarater reliability of measures (e.g., K-PeCS, ultrasound thickness measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bland–Altman analysis for measurement agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Bland–Altman plots and limits of agreement to assess agreement between raters or methods for continuous measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful complement to ICC to show systematic bias and limits of agreement (e.g., frame-based counting vs other methods). Report mean difference and 95% limits of agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability (repeatability) and use of rank correlations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stability of ratings over time using test–retest designs and nonparametric measures (e.g., Wilcoxon Spearman ρ) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate individual rater consistency on repeated identical items/images; report test–retest coefficients and consider time interval and practice effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cronbach α to assess internal consistency of a multi-item scale or global score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report α for total scales and consider subscale α; high α indicates coherence of items (e.g., CRS-R total score α = 0.973).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change (MDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report SEM and compute MDC (e.g., MDC95) to express absolute reliability and the smallest detectable individual change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important for clinical scales (e.g., Berg Balance Scale) where absolute reliability can vary across the score range; report MDC and discuss clinical interpretability and ceiling/floor effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and interpret ceiling/floor effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and report ceiling or floor effects in measurement instruments that can affect absolute reliability and sensitivity to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Berg Balance Scale shows ceiling effect near maximal scores which increases absolute reliability; discuss implications for detecting clinically important changes in individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological quality appraisal with QAREL
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the methodological quality of reliability studies using the QAREL (Quality Appraisal of Reliability Studies) tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use by independent reviewers to judge study design elements (blinding, rater selection, sample characteristics) when conducting systematic reviews of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent study selection diagrams per QUOROM/flow diagram guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a study selection flow diagram that clearly expresses the relationship between number of citations, papers, studies, and trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow QUOROM guidance: make counts unambiguous (citations vs papers vs studies vs trials); a flow diagram only makes selection transparent if it clarifies these relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define clear operational criteria and scoring definitions (calibration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and circulate annotated vignettes, rating guidelines, and initial calibration exercises so raters share a common frame of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exemplar cases and training materials (e.g., annotated vignettes for lithium response, initial review of 25 ECGs) to refine definitions and calibrate raters before formal scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training components and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Design rater training that includes rater error awareness, dimension/performance training, behavioral observation techniques, and frame-of-reference training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mixed methods (lecture, video, facilitated discussion); evaluate whether training improves interrater reliability and accuracy (evidence may be mixed). Report pre/post training ICCs and assessment of rater confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of instrument/scale format to reduce rater fatigue and ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer simpler, less fatigable instruments (e.g., binary checklists) that avoid inconsistent point conferral, but validate them against established, validated scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design simplified tools to reduce evaluator fatigue and scoring inconsistencies (e.g., CanadaWest binary scale validated against Welling); demonstrate comparable reliability and ability to discriminate experience levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple trials/averaging to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase reliability by averaging multiple repeated measurements/trials rather than relying on single trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show averaging 3 trials can produce higher interrater reliability than a single trial; report both single-trial and averaged reliability where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent validity via comparison with criterion/gold standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess concurrent validity by comparing instrument scores to objective or gold-standard measures (e.g., 3D motion analysis for posture instruments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report correlation coefficients and note items that do not align with the gold standard; use this to refine items or remove low-validity items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mixture modeling to examine score distributions and subpopulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply mixture modeling to identify latent subpopulations (e.g., full responders, partial responders, nonresponders) within score distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in large datasets for defining meaningful cutoffs or to justify continuous vs dichotomous operational definitions (example: lithium response scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define operational case definitions for outcomes (dichotomous and continuous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly specify how outcome/response is defined (e.g., A score continuous; B criteria threshold ≤4 to define responders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparing alternate operational definitions and reporting how each affects interrater reliability and ICC is important for phenotype definition in research consortia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report inter-rater reliability stratified by rater experience/training level
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and report reliability broken down by rater training or experience (e.g., fellows, residents, students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps determine whether an instrument is robust across learner levels and whether additional training/limits are needed; report ICCs or κ for each subgroup and agreement with experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess effect of additional clinical information on diagnostic agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether providing raters with extra clinical data (e.g., troponin levels) changes inter-rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report differences in κ or agreement pre- and post-unblinding; discuss potential benefits and biases introduced by unblinded information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address heterogeneity in study populations and measures before meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess heterogeneity in populations, measurement instruments, and methodological quality which may preclude quantitative pooling (meta-analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If heterogeneity is substantial, provide qualitative synthesis and explain limitations to pooling (example: ACL physical test reliability studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measurement error in units meaningful to the domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide measurement error (SEM, limits of agreement) in original measurement units (e.g., mm for ultrasound translation) and discuss clinical significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare measurement error across measurement conditions (e.g., anterior vs posterior translations) and across raters (novice vs experienced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove or revise problematic checklist items to improve reliability and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and exclude problematic questions/items from checklists that reduce inter-rater reliability or accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence shows reliability and accuracy can increase when problematic items are removed (e.g., LOTO self-audit); report item-level agreement and rationale for removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective imaging-derived measures when possible (and report software/tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer objective, image-based measures and report the imaging tools/software used (e.g., synedra View, RetCam, Fundus camera models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document image acquisition and analysis protocols and software versions to facilitate reproducibility and high inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sample size and sampling strategy for reliability studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report the number of subjects/observations, number of raters, and sampling strategy used to estimate reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small test–retest samples may yield unstable estimates (e.g., test–retest ICC based on n=11); discuss precision and confidence intervals for reliability coefficients.
